literal: They will not beg; to those who beg, they will give something without hiding, those whose nature is eating by working with their hands.
translation: Those whose nature is to eat only by working with their own hands will never beg from others; instead, they will generously give to those who ask, without hiding what they have.
modern: தன் கைகளால் உழைத்து உண்ணும் இயல்புடையவர்கள் யாரிடமும் இரந்து கேட்க மாட்டார்கள்; மாறாக, இரப்பவர்களுக்குத் தம்மிடம் உள்ளதை மறைக்காமல் கொடுப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the dignity and generosity of those who live by manual labor, specifically farmers. The phrase 'கைசெய்தூண் மாலை யவர்' refers to people whose character or habit ('மாலை') is to eat ('ஊண்') by working ('செய்து') with their own hands ('கை'). Because they are self-reliant, they will never beg ('இரவார்') from others. Instead, when others come to them seeking help, they will give ('ஈவர்') something ('ஒன்று') without concealing ('கரவாது') their resources. Through this, the poet emphasizes that honest labor not only preserves self-respect but also enables true charity.
